title: Only a logged-in owner may cancel an order: a session check that redirects, and an ownership check folded into the UPDATE's WHERE
sourceContent:
<?php
session_start();
require 'db.php';

function cancel_order(PDO $pdo, $orderId) {
    // TRAP: two gates - the session test redirects, and the ownership test is
    // hidden in the UPDATE (no row changes when the order is someone else's).
    if (empty($_SESSION['user_id'])) {
        header('Location: /login.php');
        exit;
    }
    $stmt = $pdo->prepare('UPDATE orders SET status = \'cancelled\' WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ? AND status = \'open\'');
    $stmt->execute([$orderId, $_SESSION['user_id']]);
    if ($stmt->rowCount() === 0) {
        http_response_code(403);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}
notes: A missing session redirects to /login.php (302) and stops; the ownership check is the user_id condition of the UPDATE, and a zero row count (someone else's order, or not open) answers 403. A port that moves the check into Spring Security must keep both outcomes and must not drop the user_id condition. empty($_SESSION['user_id']) also treats user id 0 / '0' as logged out.
